001: We need to define the project scope before anything else.
I agree. Without a clear scope, the team is going to get lost along the way.
So let's start by listing the main deliverables the client expects.
Good idea. I've already jotted down a few points that can serve as a basis for that list.
Perfect. After that, we'll set the deadlines for each stage.
Sounds good. I'll prepare a draft of the schedule by tomorrow.
002: Have you thought about which risks could delay our schedule?
Yes, the dependency on external suppliers is one of the biggest ones I see.
That's true. Maybe we should have a plan B for those cases.
Definitely. We can map out alternative suppliers before we start.
Great. That already reduces our margin for unexpected issues quite a bit.
I'll include that risk analysis in the project document.
003: How are we going to divide the tasks among the team members?
I think we should take each person's workload into account.
That makes sense. Some people are already overloaded with other demands.
Exactly. We can use a responsibility matrix to visualize it better.
Good suggestion. That way it's easier to avoid anyone getting overwhelmed.
I'll put that matrix together and share it with you so we can review it together.
004: Which tool do you prefer for us to track the progress of the activities?
I've been using a project management software that works really well.
The one that lets you create boards and assign tasks with deadlines?
That's the one. It also sends automatic notifications when something is late.
Sounds practical. Can you add me to the project so I can take a look?
Sure, I'll send you the invitation later today.
005: Is the budget we approved enough for all the phases of the project?
In principle, yes, but we need to monitor the costs closely.
I agree. Small expenses can add up and blow the limit at the end.
That's why I suggest we review the costs every week.
Great point. I'll create a simple report for us to record everything.
Perfect. With that control, it's easier to justify any adjustment.
006: Is the development team aligned with the requirements we defined?
I believe so, but it would be good to confirm that in a quick meeting.
True. Better to align now than to discover a mistake later on.
Exactly. I'll schedule a meeting with them for tomorrow morning.
Can you include me on the agenda so I can present the updated schedule?
No problem. I'll send you the invitation with all the details.
007: What do you think about setting intermediate milestones to validate progress?
I think it's essential. It helps us identify problems before they grow.
Right. We can define a milestone for the end of each major phase.
Good idea. That way the client can also follow the progress of the work.
I'll include those milestones in the schedule and send it to everyone.
Perfect. With that, communication with the client becomes much more transparent.
008: We need to decide who will be responsible for communication with the client.
I think it should be you, since you have more experience with him.
All right, but I'll need your support to prepare the reports.
Of course, we can put together a standard template to make that work easier.
Great. That way we keep communication consistent and professional.
Agreed. Let's define that at the next team meeting.
009: What will we do if the client asks for changes in the middle of the project?
We need to have a clear process to assess the impact of those changes.
I agree. Each request should go through a cost and timeline analysis.
And if it's something simple, we can approve it quickly without red tape.
Yes, but everything should be documented to avoid misunderstandings.
Perfect. I'll draft a change management policy for us to follow.
010: Do you think we can deliver the project within the stipulated deadline?
If we keep the current pace and no major unexpected issues come up, yes.
I hope so. But it's good to have a safety margin in the schedule.
I agree. We can set aside a few extra days for possible final adjustments.
Good idea. That gives us more peace of mind to deliver quality work.
I'll adjust the schedule with that margin and share it with the team.
